population.adaptation: Typed limit, missing-value and OOB policies retain source populations and callback order; registered operations receive complete vectors.

categorical-population.adaptation: Owned category catalogs retain unused and missing levels; continuous limits control the positional projection.

expansion.adaptation: Typed paired multiplicative/additive expansion and blank-layer domain contributions.

break-selection.adaptation: Default, hidden, explicit or registered vector selection retains NULL/empty distinctions, complete transformed/inverse batch context, source coordinates and named metadata. Explicit, coupled-label and minor paths share the same computation.

labels.adaptation: Typed formatter resources and registered vector label operations preserve pre-filter candidates, names and source type metadata.

calendar.adaptation: Explicit calendar/timezone/locale resources and typed width/format specifications replace R process state.

transformation.adaptation: Resolved built-in or registered transform/rescaler descriptors replace aliases and closures; batch and NULL protocols preserve ordered computation.

bins.adaptation: Typed bin closure, count policy and interval endpoint selection share the mapped scale pipeline.
bins.boundary: Selection and labels are GG-04; stepped/interval guide painting is GG-05.

palette-selection.adaptation: Explicit palette/scale descriptors and owned theme resources preserve explicit/theme/fallback/default precedence; registered palette operations replace R function forms.

manual-and-range.adaptation: Typed named/unnamed palette vectors, numeric ranges and gradient knot vectors retain independent cardinality and missing lookup rules.

gradient.adaptation: Resolved gradient descriptor carries colors, midpoint, stops and interpolation space; spelling aliases do not create separate computations.

palette-parameters.adaptation: Reference hue/grey/Brewer/viridis policies use shared color kernels and explicit catalog/parameter values.

size-and-shape.adaptation: Area/radius/size and solid/hollow shape policies are authored explicitly and use the same mark/guide mapping.

secondary.adaptation: Typed duplicate, monotone transformed or registered secondary guides retain source candidates and label callback metadata.
secondary.boundary: Secondary candidate/label computation is GG-04; guide title/layout composition is GG-05.

channels.adaptation: Shared typed scale identity trains the selected channels over the same source population.

guide-selection.adaptation: Typed hidden/legend/colorbar/bins/steps selection retains scale-side candidate, mapped key, ramp and label computation.
guide-selection.boundary: Rendering, title callbacks, key collection, ordering and placement are GG-05; scale-side selection is covered here.

guide-presentation.adaptation: Owned guide title and placement descriptors replace R objects; title callbacks and full placement/composition belong to GG-05.

syntax.adaptation: Deprecated names and R call diagnostics are language syntax. Meaningful forwarded computation is expressed by the corresponding typed descriptor above. Native validation replaces R argument matching.

extension-class.adaptation: Built-in families select shared training/mapping policies. Registered operations implement computations; custom class authoring belongs to GG-16.

typed-dispatch.adaptation: Typed columns, scale descriptors and named limit/domain-contribution builders replace R S3 data dispatch and variadic lims calls.

lifecycle.adaptation: Owned immutable prepared state and fresh training replace mutable R range/cache reset and clone; replacement versus fresh batches and retained captures are checked by the actual-host runner. Internal cache identity is not a public R-object promise.

field_stage_contract.adaptation: Typed staged aesthetics train scaled statistic outputs; scale computation consumes the shared staged population.
